plan.contextChunk: This figure shows a single right triangle drawn in plain black outline with no axes, grid, or shading. The triangle sits on a horizontal base labeled a beneath its midpoint. From the right end of that base a vertical side rises, labeled p on its outer edge. The hypotenuse slants down from the top of the vertical side to the left vertex, labeled h above its middle. A small open square at the lower right vertex marks the right angle between the base and the vertical side, and a single arc at the left vertex marks the acute angle, labeled with the Greek letter theta. The labeling is organized around theta rather than around the page: a is adjacent to theta, p is opposite it, and h is the hypotenuse, so each name states a role rather than a direction. Carrying no numbers at all, the drawing serves as the reference diagram for recovering an unknown acute angle from two known side lengths, the given pair determining which inverse trigonometric relation applies.

interactionPlan.concept: The labels a, p, h are not directions but roles (adjacent, opposite, hypotenuse) defined relative to the reference angle θ, and a known ratio of two sides recovers θ through the inverse trigonometric function.
elements: horizontal base side labeled a beneath its midpoint
vertical right side labeled p on its outer (right) edge
slanted hypotenuse labeled h above its midpoint
small open square marking the right angle at the lower-right vertex
angle arc at the left vertex labeled with the Greek letter θ
role caption (adjacent / opposite / hypotenuse) that appears next to a clicked side
highlight styling (e.g. blue stroke) applied to the selected side and to the θ arc
relation badge naming the matching trig ratio (sin θ, cos θ, or tan θ) when a ratio is entered

interactions.teaches: Clicking a, p, or h highlights that side together with θ and captions it adjacent, opposite, or hypotenuse — making explicit that these names describe a side's role relative to θ, not a fixed direction on the page.

interactions.label: Angle θ
interactions.teaches: Dragging θ reshapes the right triangle — the opposite side p grows relative to the adjacent side a as θ increases — while the labels a, p, h keep their roles, showing that the angle controls the opposite-to-adjacent balance.

interactions.label: Known side ratio
interactions.teaches: Typing a ratio of two sides (p/h, p/a, a/h, ...) names the trig function it equals (sin, tan, cos), and supplying its numeric value makes the inverse function set θ and reshape the triangle — known side lengths determine the unknown angle.

demo_steps.title: Name the roles
demo_steps.narration: Click each side in turn: a is captioned adjacent, p opposite, h hypotenuse, each highlighted alongside θ. The names are roles relative to θ, not page directions.

demo_steps.title: Angle drives the ratio
demo_steps.narration: Drag θ larger and watch p stretch while a shrinks; the same three role labels stay put, so the angle alone sets the opposite-to-adjacent balance.

demo_steps.title: Ratio drives the angle (inverse)
demo_steps.narration: Now read the triangle backwards: enter a ratio such as p/h = 0.6 and the figure snaps θ to arcsin(0.6) ≈ 37° and lights the sine relation — a known pair of sides pins down the unknown angle.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The same right triangle can be read in two directions: θ fixes the side ratios (forward trig), and a known side ratio fixes θ (inverse trig) — with a, p, h always meaning adjacent, opposite, hypotenuse relative to θ.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Plain black-outline right triangle on a blank background, no axes or grid. Base horizontal with label a centered below it; vertical side on the right with label p just outside it; hypotenuse slanting from the top-right vertex down to the left vertex with label h above its midpoint. Draw a small open square at the lower-right corner for the right angle and a single arc with θ at the left vertex. On click, recolor the chosen side and the θ arc in a clear accent (e.g. blue) and place the role word (adjacent/opposite/hypotenuse) beside that side. When a ratio is entered, show a small badge near θ naming sin θ / cos θ / tan θ and reshape the triangle to the inverse-trig angle. Keep all geometry consistent: vertical side = h·sin θ, base = h·cos θ, so the slider and the equation_input drive the identical triangle.

authoredContext:
Given two sides of a right triangle like the one shown in the figure, find an angle.

An illustration of a right triangle with an angle theta. Adjacent to theta is the side a, opposite theta is the side p, and the hypoteneuse is side h.
